values.note: Reservations online (Polk County's WebTrac site) or in person; the county also says 'All campgrounds are first-come, first-served.' 14 consecutive days, then 28 days away from that campground; 100 days a year across all county campgrounds. One camping unit and up to four people per site.

booking.source: https://www.polkfl.gov/things-to-do/parks-and-recreation/campgrounds/ ('All campgrounds are first-come, first-served. Reservations can be made online or in-person.'; 'The maximum stay is 14 consecutive days, after which the camper must vacate that particular campground for 28 days') + WebTrac (Saddle Creek sites for rent online), read 2026-10-21

note: Polk County campground at 750-acre Saddle Creek Park, Lakeland; loop in an oak hammock near the back of the park among former-phosphate-pit lakes. Reopened Oct 2024 after hurricane closures. The low RV Life rating reflects dated reviews of an aging bathhouse, not a closure. No campfires at Saddle Creek; after-hours entry must be pre-scheduled with the resident park caretaker (Polk County rules, read 2026-10-21). --Claude
summary: Confirmed 20/30/50-amp + water, showers, dump, 14-night max. Changed sites 54 -> 41 (36 RV + 5 tent-only primitive). Added $20/night (water+electric; the $10 primitive sites are tent only), flush toilets, online booking on the county's WebTrac site. Not stated by the county: max rig length (the note-derived 30 ft left), season. Note cleaned of field facts.
flags: The county's 2025 rules page still says 'No reservations until more reliable internet becomes available. Campgrounds will remain first-come, first-served', while the current campgrounds page and WebTrac sell sites online.
